FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.subtitle: Everything you need to know about ZenOTA.

q1.q: Do I need to eject my Expo app?
q1.a: No! ZenOTA works seamlessly with managed Expo workflows. It uses the exact same expo-updates library you already have installed. You just point the configuration to our servers in your app.json.

q2.q: What happens if an update crashes my app?
q2.a: By default, the Expo Updates runtime will detect a fatal crash on startup and automatically roll back to the previously embedded bundle, ensuring your users are never stuck on a broken screen.

q3.a: A deployment is a single push of a new bundle (using zenota publish). If you publish an update for both iOS and Android simultaneously, it counts as one deployment. There are no limits on how many users can download your updates.

prerequisites.title: Prerequisites
prerequisites.subtitle: Configure your Expo project for OTA updates before using ZenOTA.
prerequisites.desc: ZenOTA replaces the default EAS Update endpoint with its own. For this to work, you need the <codeTag>expo-updates</codeTag> library installed and the update configuration initialized in your project.
prerequisites.step2Desc: This will add a <codeTag>runtimeVersion</codeTag> and an <codeTag>updates.url</codeTag> field to your <codeTag>app.json</codeTag>.
prerequisites.step3Desc: Finally, you'll need to update the <codeTag>updates.url</codeTag> in your <codeTag>app.json</codeTag> to point to your ZenOTA manifest endpoint.
prerequisites.critical: <bold>Critical:</bold> You must complete these steps <bold>before</bold> installing the ZenOTA CLI. Without <codeTag>expo-updates</codeTag>, the CLI export command will fail.

quickstart.title: Quick Start
quickstart.subtitle: Ship your first update in under 5 minutes.

1.title: Install the ZenOTA CLI
1.desc: Install the CLI globally via npm or yarn.

2.title: Generate an API Key
2.desc: Go to your Dashboard → CLI Access Tokens → Generate New Key. Copy the key immediately — it won't be shown again.

3.title: Authenticate the CLI
3.desc: Run the login command and paste your API key when prompted.

4.title: Publish your update
4.desc: Navigate to your Expo project root. Run publish and choose your target platform (Android, iOS, or both) from the interactive menu.

apiKeys.title: API Keys
apiKeys.subtitle: Secure your CLI deployments with scoped API tokens.

warning.title: One-time display policy
warning.desc: API keys are only shown once at creation time. Copy and store them in a secure place (e.g., a password manager or CI/CD secret store). If you lose a key, you must revoke and regenerate it.

steps: Go to your Dashboard → CLI Access Tokens.
Click "Generate New Key". The raw key is shown only once.
Run `zenota login` in your terminal and paste the key when prompted.
The CLI stores the key securely in ~/.zenota-config.json.

manifest.title: Manifest & Versioning
manifest.subtitle: How ZenOTA matches updates to native builds.
manifest.desc: ZenOTA generates <bold>Expo-compatible manifests</bold>. Your app's native build must have a matching <codeTag>runtimeVersion</codeTag> configured in <codeTag>app.json</codeTag> for an update to be applied.
manifest.proTip: <bold>Pro Tip:</bold> Use the <codeTag>sdkVersion</codeTag> policy during development and switch to a <codeTag>nativeVersion</codeTag> policy for production after your first App Store submission.
